text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet ordered the minister in charge of the civil secret services to review the activities of the Intelligence Office. The cabinet is to convene a national agrarian round-table conference on April 25-26.

- The presidential board of the National Federation of Hungarian Farmers' Associations in a letter to the prime minister asked for corrections in the amendment to the social insurance act. Meanwhile, the president of the Agricultural Producers' Advocacy Organisation announced a mass rally for farmers to be staged in Budapest on April 4.
- Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea received Hungarian Democratic Forume president Sandor Lezsak in Bucharest.
- After stagnation in 1966, Hungary's GDP is expected to grow in 1997, along with domestic demand, analysts at Budapest Bank conclude in a study.
- Hungary's joining the OECD a year ago contributed to last year's rocketing share prices on the Budapest Stock Exchange, said Minister of Industry Szabolcs Fazakas.
- Two Austrian journalists posing as Serbian drug traffickers had themselves smuggled over the Austrian-Hungarian border. Border guards on both sides apparently cooperated with the smugglers.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- The Socialist and Free Democrat coalition in City Hall approved the privatisation contract of the Budapest Water Works.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Free Democrat president Ivan Peto said that Slovakia continues to produce drafts that not only fail to stabilise the present situation but worsen it, particularly as regards the education of ethnic Hungarians in Slovakia and issues affecting the use of language.

- Visiting US Senator Joseph Biden said that NATO membership entails not only rights but major commitments, and America wants to see the states seeking membership ready to sacrifice more of their budgets toward defence spending and contribute to NATO operations like that in Bosnia.

- The gap between the rich and the poor in Hungary continues to widen: the 20 percent of people with the highest incomes earn four times as much as the poorest 20 percent, according to a fresh report by the Central Statistical Office.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Minister of Industry Szabolcs confirmed Thursday that Russian Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov is holding talks in Budapest on repayment of the remaining instalment of the Russian state debt.
- Douglas Miller, Vice President of the Lockheed Martin Corp. said in Budapest on Thursday that the company which produces F-16 fighter planes is ready to propose a joint business deal to Hungary.
- The 23 Hungarian companies in which the German electronics concern Siemens has stakes took in an aggregate HUF 59.3 billion in revenues last year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
The proportion of agricultural workers and producers approving of the country's membership in the EU fell from 40 percent in 1996 to only 12 percent this year, according to a poll.
- Matav signed a contract with Digital Hungary Kft to upgrade Metav's network management system.
- The Finnish-Japanese consortium Ivo Tomen plans to invest $100 million in the power plant Budapesti Eromu over the next few years.
